Riley (AE): Heads-up — ACME wants numbers for an enterprise commit. They asked for reserved GPU sizing, autoscale policy, preheat/KV warmup, and a fallback pricing path. Meeting tomorrow to finalize presales. Traffic callouts: 200 RPS steady, 1,200 RPS 1-min spikes, median 30 tokens/request, three model tiers: llama2-70b-q4 (primary), redwood-rl-13b (fallback), tiny-embed for embeddings. They want a hard monthly cost cap and automatic fallback to cheaper model if P95 latency > 300ms. Also hitting our security questionnaire: KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs. @Sam @Maya @Arjun can you comment quick so I can reply to their procurement team? :pray:

Sam (Solutions): Quick Qs: is 200 RPS measured as requests/sec or user sessions? and are spikes predictable (cron) or ad-hoc?

Riley (AE): 200 RPS is steady arrival rate. Spikes are ad-hoc, usually triggered by marketing promos. They care about 99th latency during spikes.

Sam (Solutions): OK. Rough capacity calc (very rough):
```
30 tokens/req * 200 req/s = 6000 tokens/s baseline
30 tokens/req * 1200 req/s = 36000 tokens/s peak
```
Serving notes: llama2-70b-q4 on H100 (or equivalent) with batching/continuous-KV gives best latency. For baseline I'd plan for reserved capacity sized to cover ~95% of load (headroom for autoscale). For spikes, use burst credits + reserved autoscale to add nodes. Recommend autoscale policy: min nodes = cover 200 RPS baseline, burst pool = +2-4 nodes, scale cooldown 30s-60s.

Arjun (Infra): Converting to nodes: with our perf profiles, one H100-backed serving pod (optimized) covers ~80-120 RPS for small-ish completions (30 tokens median) with batching. So baseline 200 RPS -> reserve 2 pods (prefer 3 for headroom). Spikes to 1200 -> need ~10-12 pods total.

Arjun (Infra): Proposal: reserved pool = 3 H100 pods (reserved GPUs) + 2 A10G pods for embeddings and lower-tier models. Burst/autoscale should be able to add up to 9 additional H100 pods from burst pool (on-demand/spot depending on region) with routing policy to shed to redwood-rl-13b when capacity constrained.

Maya (PM): From product/economics perspective: two pressure points to control cost: quantized variants and routing policies. Recommend pre-negotiated fallback path: when P95 > 300ms for >15s, route new requests to redwood-rl-13b-q4_k on A10G (cheaper but slightly lower quality). Also enable prefix/KV caching and cache warmup window.

Maya (PM): Preheat plan: schedule rolling preheat for peak windows and run a short synthetic warmup that exercises top 50 prompts. For KV-heavy workloads, we should run warmup traffic per-AZ post-deploy. Add a canary rollout (5% traffic) for 10m before full switch.

Beth (Security): Security Qs: KMS integration is supported (we have customer-managed KMS + HSM option). For VPC: private control plane + VPC peering is possible, we provide audit logs to S3 and CloudWatch. We need to confirm data residency in the questionnaire — which region do they require? Also ask if they need sub-second audit log retention or longer.

Riley (AE): ACME needs EU residency and 12 months audit retention. Also they asked whether secrets rotation during preheat affects warm caches.

Arjun (Infra): Secrets rotation doesn't invalidate KV cache but will trigger redeploys if keys change for the control plane. Recommendation: rotate keys off-peak and run a short re-warm sequence. For preheat we can take a warm snapshot of frequent KV entries and prime on deploy.

Sam (Solutions): Pricing sketch (order-of-magnitude for presales):
- Reserved 3 H100 + 2 A10G pool + burst capacity -> estimated committed monthly cost ~ $72k-$95k depending on region and commitment term.
- PAYG for same traffic roughly $110k-$140k/month (wide range due to tokens and burst).
We should present both: committed tier (with reserved pool + burst credits) and a capped fallback (routing to redwood-rl-13b when cost or latency thresholds exceed).

Maya (PM): Also propose Optimize run: run quantization suggestions for llama2-70b to see if q4_k maintains quality — that could reduce reserved capacity by ~20%. Worth running a quick evaluate + A/B on the canary.

Riley (AE): Great. Action items I need to take to ACME by EOD today: 1) send proposed reserved config+pricing range, 2) give autoscale + fallback policy doc, 3) attach security notes about KMS/VPC and confirm EU region + audit retention. Who will provide the sizing calc and final numbers?

Arjun (Infra): I can produce a 1-page sizing calc with node counts, expected RPS per pod, and warmup steps (will include conservative and aggressive variants). Deliver by 3pm PT.

Sam (Solutions): I'll draft the autoscale policy text (min/reserved, burst, cooldowns, fallback trigger) and example JSON policy for the presales doc. Deliver by 2pm PT.

Beth (Security): I'll export the standard KMS/VPC answers and note the EU residency piece; confirm retention details. Deliver by 4pm PT.

Maya (PM): I'll run a quick Optimize quantization check and give an expected %capacity reduction estimate. Deliver by 5pm PT (might be best-effort).

Riley (AE): Perfect. I'll stitch together the email to ACME and propose a 9am ET presales call tomorrow. Thanks everyone :rocket:

deploy-bot: Deployment check — no active incidents in eu-west-1, spot capacity available for burst pools (may be preemptible).

Riley (AE): added: please tag the presales doc with the recommended SLA clause for reserved pools (90% uptime, with credit tiers) and include a short paragraph on how fallback affects SLOs.

Sam (Solutions): noted. I'll add the SLA blurb and a small matrix showing cost vs latency trade-offs.

Riley (AE): Thanks — closing this thread, will ping when I send the email to ACME.
